s1.syndrome_frame: Sepsis with skin and soft tissue infection
salient_findings: Skin ulceration in the left upper limb
Lethargy and fever for 1 day
Large areas of fluid exudation and local tension blisters on the left hand and forearm
Dark purple ecchymoses at the base of the left hand and forearm
Extensive swelling from proximal middle segment to wrist
key_facts: 85-year-old man
Admitted due to skin ulceration, lethargy, and fever
Stabbed in the left upper limb while cleaning sea shrimps
Developed drowsiness and fever with a maximum body temperature of 38.8°C
History of diabetes for more than 20 years
Long-term history of alcoholism
White blood cell count: 11.77 × 10^9/L
Procalcitonin: > 100 ng/mL
Lactate: 4.28 mmol/L
Blood culture: Positive for Gram-negative bacilli
Microscopic examination showed comma-like, flagellate, spore-free bacteria

shortlist.label: Vibrio vulnificus infection
shortlist.why_kept: Patient was stabbed in the left upper limb while cleaning sea shrimps, and blood culture showed Gram-negative bacilli, which is consistent with Vibrio vulnificus infection

shortlist.label: Necrotizing fasciitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presented with skin ulceration, lethargy, and fever, and laboratory tests showed elevated white blood cell count, procalcitonin, and lactate, which are indicative of necrotizing fasciitis

shortlist.label: Sepsis due to Gram-negative bacilli
shortlist.why_kept: Blood culture was positive for Gram-negative bacilli, and patient presented with symptoms of sepsis, including fever, lethargy, and elevated white blood cell count

shortlist.label: Vibrio parahaemolyticus infection
shortlist.why_kept: Similar to Vibrio vulnificus, Vibrio parahaemolyticus is a Gram-negative bacillus that can cause infection through exposure to contaminated seafood

shortlist.label: Severe soft tissue infection
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presented with extensive swelling, tension blisters, and dark purple ecchymoses on the left upper limb, which are indicative of a severe soft tissue infection

raw.rationale: The patient was stabbed in the left upper limb while cleaning sea shrimps, which is a common route of exposure for Vibrio vulnificus, and the laboratory tests showed Gram-negative bacilli with comma-like, flagellate, spore-free bacteria, consistent with Vibrio vulnificus

rejected.label: Necrotizing fasciitis
rejected.why: While the patient has skin ulceration and swelling, the presence of Gram-negative bacilli and the exposure to sea shrimps points more specifically to Vibrio vulnificus infection

rejected.label: Sepsis due to Gram-negative bacilli
rejected.why: The diagnosis is too broad and does not account for the specific exposure to sea shrimps and the characteristic bacteria morphology

rejected.label: Vibrio parahaemolyticus infection
rejected.why: Vibrio parahaemolyticus typically causes gastrointestinal symptoms, which are not mentioned in the vignette, and the bacteria morphology is more consistent with Vibrio vulnificus

rejected.label: Severe soft tissue infection
rejected.why: This diagnosis is too general and does not account for the specific cause of the infection, which is likely Vibrio vulnificus given the exposure and laboratory results
